thread:
sam (new-dev): Hey folks — following the Windows quickstart guide. First call returns 403 with body: `{'error':'workspace_limited','msg':'limited workspace'}`. I put REDWOOD_API_KEY into Windows env via setx and restarted powershell.

rachel (devex): Welcome! Which sample image are you using? The Windows quickstart has two variants (native and WSL).

sam (new-dev): Using `quickstart-windows` (native). Command from README: `.
run-quickstart.ps1 -Key $env:REDWOOD_API_KEY`. The app logs show `no token detected` before the 403.

dom (sdk): FYI there's a known parity issue where the native Windows wrapper script was reading `RW_KEY` by mistake. The SDK inside logs `Authorization` missing then the server returns workspace_limited. Try echoing the env inside the process: `Write-Output $env:REDWOOD_API_KEY` in the same session the app runs.

sam (new-dev): Confirmed the env is present in my user session but the quickstart service runs as a scheduled task under a different user so the env wasn't visible there. I switched it to the same user and restarted the service.

infra-bot: Auto: Detected scheduled task `redwood-quickstart` running as `SYSTEM`.

lee (billing): I checked your org `sam-win-test` and billing status: "Limited - payment info missing". That will also produce workspace_limited for write endpoints. We can enable a 48h dev unlock if you want.

sam (new-dev): Oh — I closed the add-billing SSO earlier because it redirected. Looks like that left the workspace limited.

dom (sdk): Two quick SDK fixes: (1) add a clear diagnostic when env var missing in scheduled-task contexts, (2) surface `workspace_limited` with a one-line actionable like "Add payment method or request dev unlock". I'll open SDK issue.

rachel (devex): I'll patch the Windows quickstart README to warn about scheduled tasks/Windows services not inheriting user env vars and pin the sample to SDK >=0.10.5 which contains the clearer error message. Also adding a troubleshooting note about SSO/billing modal.

lee (billing): I enabled a 48h dev unlock for `sam-win-test`. You should be able to call in ~30s. Also sent DM with billing completion steps.

sam (new-dev): Switched the service user and retried after unlock. First call now returns 200. Thanks everyone!

rachel (devex): Nice. Follow-ups: README PR to call out Windows scheduled task env gotcha, SDK issue for clearer diagnostics, and a tiny sample script to print env at startup.

sam (new-dev): I'll open the README PR with the sample env-check script. Saving this thread for anyone hitting Windows scheduled-task + billing traps. :white_check_mark:
__notes: Slack thread export. Messages are chronological and each message prefixed with sender display names.
